options.text: There's no task.expirationHandler set, and no handling for the task being interrupted mid-cleanup — if the system revokes the task's time before the cleanup finishes, the work is killed with no chance to save partial progress
BGProcessingTask cannot call setTaskCompleted at all
The function name performExpensiveDatabaseCleanup is too long to compile
task.setTaskCompleted must always be called with success: false

explanation: Background tasks can be cut off before they finish if the system needs the time back. Without an expirationHandler to react to that (cancel gracefully, save progress, or at least call setTaskCompleted(success: false)), a long operation can be killed mid-work with no cleanup.

prompt: A platform team wants to catch accessibility regressions — like missing VoiceOver labels — automatically before merge, across dozens of feature teams. What scales better than relying solely on manual QA passes?

options.text: Automated accessibility audits in UI tests (e.g. Xcode's accessibility audit APIs) run in CI on every pull request
Requiring every engineer to personally test with VoiceOver enabled for their entire workday
Accepting that accessibility issues cannot be detected by any automated tooling
Disabling Dynamic Type support so text size never changes

explanation: Automated accessibility auditing in CI catches many common issues (missing labels, insufficient contrast, small tap targets) on every PR, well before a manual pass would — manual testing still matters, but doesn't scale to every change on its own.

prompt: Xcode's String Catalog (.xcstrings) format can flag a translated string as 'stale.' What does that mean?

options.text: Xcode detected that the source code reference for that string appears to have disappeared, suggesting it may no longer be used and is a candidate for cleanup
The string's translation is more than a year old and needs re-translation
The string contains a typo detected by spell-check
The string exceeds the maximum character length for its UI element

explanation: String Catalogs track where each string is referenced from source. When Xcode can no longer find a reference to a string, it marks the entry stale — a signal it may be dead content worth removing, across a codebase too large to audit by hand.

prompt: A team is bringing an existing iPad-optimized SwiftUI app to visionOS. What's a common architecture adjustment planned beyond simply recompiling?

options.text: Auditing fixed pixel-based layout assumptions and hard-coded 2D interaction patterns, since visionOS adds depth, window-based multitasking by default, and different default view styles the iPad layout doesn't anticipate
visionOS cannot run any code written in SwiftUI
visionOS requires the entire app to be rewritten in RealityKit with no UIKit or SwiftUI involvement
visionOS apps cannot share any code with the iPad target

explanation: A SwiftUI app can often run on visionOS with real code sharing, but layout and interaction assumptions tuned for a flat iPad screen (fixed sizes, 2D-only gestures) usually need real auditing for a spatial, windowed environment.

prompt: A WidgetKit widget and its containing app can share mutable state directly in memory, the same way two view controllers in the same app process can.

options.text: True
False

explanation: A widget extension runs in its own separate process from the host app — they don't share memory. State has to go through an out-of-process mechanism, like an App Group's shared UserDefaults or files, and the widget's timeline must be explicitly reloaded (e.g. WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines) to reflect the change.

prompt: A persistence layer used by millions of installed users needs a breaking schema change. What's the standard approach to avoid data loss or crashes on upgrade?

options.text: Ship a versioned, staged migration — such as a Core Data/SwiftData migration mapping model, or an equivalent manual step — that transforms the on-disk store the first time the updated app launches
Ship the new schema and instruct users to delete and reinstall the app
Schema changes are not possible once an app has shipped to the App Store
Rely on iCloud to automatically rewrite the on-disk format for every user simultaneously

explanation: A versioned migration path lets each user's device transform its own existing data to the new schema on next launch, without any data loss or requiring a fresh install.

prompt: Core Data's lightweight migration can automatically infer a migration mapping for many common schema changes, but a sufficiently complex transformation — like splitting one entity into two, or transforming stored values — generally requires a custom, heavyweight mapping model.

options.text: True
False

explanation: Lightweight migration covers straightforward cases Core Data can infer on its own, like adding an attribute or a hinted rename. Structural changes that aren't a simple one-to-one mapping need an explicit mapping model with custom migration policies.

prompt: A platform team designs an analytics pipeline under strict data-minimization requirements. Which practice best reflects 'privacy by design' for that pipeline?

options.text: Collecting and transmitting only the specific fields needed for a defined analytics purpose decided at design time, rather than logging broad raw data and filtering later
Collecting every available device signal up front in case it's useful for a future feature
Storing analytics data indefinitely by default to avoid ever needing to reprocess it
Sending analytics data unencrypted to reduce CPU overhead

explanation: Privacy by design means deciding what's actually needed before collecting anything, not hoovering up everything available and figuring out the privacy implications afterward.

prompt: A platform team sets a 99.7% crash-free-sessions SLO as a release-blocking gate. What typically happens when a release candidate exceeds that threshold (worse than 99.7%)?

options.text: The release is held back from wider rollout — or an active rollout is paused or rolled back — until the regression causing the extra crashes is found and fixed
The SLO is purely informational and has no effect on ship decisions
It automatically extends the App Store review time
Crash reporting is disabled for the next release to hide the metric

explanation: A release-blocking SLO exists precisely to stop a regression from reaching the full user base — exceeding it triggers holding or rolling back the release until the cause is addressed.

prompt: Apple Push Notification service (APNs) guarantees that a notification sent while a device is offline will always be delivered the instant the device reconnects, with no possibility of coalescing or dropping.

options.text: True
False

explanation: APNs makes a best-effort delivery attempt, not a strict guarantee — it can coalesce multiple pending notifications for the same app and can drop ones that go undelivered long enough. Time-sensitive data shouldn't rely solely on push delivery timing.

prompt: Why would a platform team migrate an app's background-refresh logic from the legacy UIApplication background fetch API to the BackgroundTasks framework (BGAppRefreshTask / BGProcessingTask)?

options.text: BackgroundTasks is the modern, more capable replacement — it supports longer-running processing tasks with explicit constraints like requiring power or network, and the older fetch API is effectively legacy for new work
The legacy API was removed entirely and no longer exists in any SDK
BackgroundTasks is only available to App Clips, not full apps
The legacy API runs tasks on the main thread with no possibility of doing work in the background

explanation: BackgroundTasks gives finer-grained control — separate request types for quick refreshes versus longer processing work, with explicit constraints the system can use to schedule more intelligently — than the older fetch-interval API.

prompt: Two internal teams communicate through a shared internal Swift Package's public API. What's a practical CI safeguard against an accidental breaking change to that API?

options.text: An API-diffing or binary-compatibility check that compares the current public interface against the previous release and fails the build if a breaking change is introduced without an intentional version bump
Trusting that engineers will remember to manually check every consumer before changing anything
Making every symbol in the package public and open by default so nothing can technically 'break'
Removing all documentation so consumers can't depend on documented behavior

explanation: Automated interface-diffing catches an accidental breaking change (a removed method, a changed signature) at the moment it's introduced, rather than relying on every engineer to remember every downstream consumer by hand.
